findings.issue_text: [BUG] The MeetLocationType guard destructures `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then unconditionally reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, so a null or empty destinationCalendar throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. Any CalendarEvent built with `destinationCalendar: []` or null (which this very diff introduces in packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, handleCancelBooking.ts and confirm.handler.ts) crashes the location-resolution step of EventManager whenever Google Meet location needs the fallback check; previously the `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` optional chain made this path safe. Payment-success and reschedule flows that pass empty arrays now 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback branch searches `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` with a falsy `externalCalendarId`, so the lookup can never match and `selectedCalendar` is always undefined in that branch. When updateEvent is invoked without an externalCalendarId (EventManager's updateAllCalendarEvents passes `calenderExternalId` which is null when the booking reference has no stored external id), the previous fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is destroyed and Google's events.update is called with `calendarId: undefined`, causing the update to fail with a 404/bad-request instead of updating the host's calendar event.

[BUG] In deleteEvent the fallback branch evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` where `externalCalendarId` is undefined, so the find matches nothing and `calendarId` becomes undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks an externalCalendarId (the normal case for legacy bookings created before externalCalendarId was persisted, or collective bookings created by the non-credentialId branch that returns `externalId: undefined`) now calls Google events.delete with `calendarId: undefined` and the remote event is never deleted, leaving orphaned calendar events on every such cancellation.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently drops all team members' destination calendars when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null (no eventType.destinationCalendar and no organizerUser.destinationCalendar), because optional chaining short-circuits the push. For a COLLECTIVE event type where neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar configured but individual hosts do, the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are computed and then discarded; createAllCalendarEvents then takes the null-destination fallback path and the hosts' calendars never receive the booking, contradicting the PR's stated purpose of handling collective multiple-host destination calendars.

[BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents the `credential` variable is declared outside the reference loop and is only conditionally reassigned, so when a reference's credentialId resolves to nothing (not in this.calendarCredentials and no DB row with app?.slug), the stale credential from the previous iteration (or undefined on the first iteration) is passed to `updateEvent(credential, event, ...)`. With multiple calendar references on one booking, a missing second-host credential causes the second reference to be updated against the first host's credential (writing to the wrong calendar) or, on the first iteration, against undefined, which crashes when CalendarManager's updateEvent dereferences the credential — in both cases the second host's calendar event is left stale.

[BUG] createEvent now resolves the target calendar solely via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, so any destination calendar whose credentialId is unset or does not match the credential executing the call falls through to `calendarId: "primary"`. Pre-refactor destination calendars (and the no-credentialId branch of createAllCalendarEvents that calls `createEvent(c, event)` without a matching destination) silently switch from creating events in the user's selected sub-calendar (the old `destinationCalendar?.externalId` behavior) to creating them in the Google account's primary calendar, misplacing bookings with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] The new `user.destinationCalendar` access inside teamMemberPromises assumes the loaded user objects include the destinationCalendar relation, but the rewritten loadUsers for the eventTypeId path returns hosts from the eventType query and for the dynamic path selects `{...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true}`; nothing in this diff guarantees `destinationCalendar` is part of those selects. If the underlying user select does not include destinationCalendar, `user.destinationCalendar` is undefined for every host and `teamDestinationCalendars` stays empty on all collective bookings — the entire feature silently no-ops with no error, and reviewers/operators only discover it from missing calendar events.

[ADVISORY] The DB credential fallback is gated on `credentialFromDB.app?.slug`, so any credential row whose app relation is absent (legacy/seeded credentials or credentials created before the app-store migration) is skipped and the destination is silently not created against. Bookings for such credentials complete without a calendar event and without any logged error or user-facing warning, because the `if (credential)` guard simply skips the createEvent call; operators debugging missing calendar events get no signal that the credential was dropped here.

[BUG] The rewritten Meet-location check dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without optional chaining, so a booking with location integrations:google-video and no destination calendar crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration'). Any booking where eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are both absent (handleNewBooking sets destinationCalendar to null in exactly that case, per its own ternary) and the location is Google Meet throws a 500 at EventManager.create instead of the previous behavior of falling back to Cal Video; the old code's `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` tolerated the null.

[BUG] The conditional was inverted: the old `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` (slug written only when billing is disabled) became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` (slug written only when billing is enabled), and the metadata.requestedSlug condition was flipped the same way. Self-hosted installs (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false) now create organizations with no slug and no requestedSlug, breaking org URLs and later slug resolution; on billing-enabled deployments the slug is now persisted at creation time before payment, breaking the paywall flow where the slug was only requested in metadata and assigned after checkout.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback branch evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` where externalCalendarId is by definition falsy (that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId ?` failed), so the find compares against undefined and never matches. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, selectedCalendar resolves to undefined instead of the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so the calendar update is issued against the wrong calendar (or undefined calendarId) and the reschedule silently fails or corrupts the wrong event.

[BUG] deleteEvent copies the same broken pattern: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate compares against undefined and can never match a real calendar. Cancellation of a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId passes calendarId=undefined to calendar.events.delete, so the remote calendar event is never deleted and orphaned events accumulate in users' calendars.

[BUG] Only the BOOKING_REJECTED describe's expected payload was updated to `destinationCalendar: []`; the other webhook scenarios in this same file assert the pre-change single-object/null destinationCalendar shape and were not updated. The sibling webhook e2e scenarios fail in CI against the new array-valued payload, the same sibling-miss pattern as leaving one flag checked on a shared serialization path while its neighbors on the identical payload builder go unexamined.

[ADVISORY] The rewritten createAllCalendarEvents multi-destination loop, the new prisma.credential.findUnique credential-from-DB fallback, and the credentialId-matching logic in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent have no test coverage anywhere in this diff. The only test touched is webhook.e2e.ts's payload-shape expectation; a regression in the destination loop (e.g., skipping a member's calendar or double-creating events) or in the DB credential fallback (which silently skips creation when app?.slug is missing) ships undetected and surfaces only as users' missing calendar events in production.

[ADVISORY] The multi-destination matching (create against the calendar whose credentialId matches the calling credential) was implemented only in GoogleCalendarService; Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still blindly destructure the first element (`[mainHostDestinationCalendar]`) and ignore which credential is executing. For a COLLECTIVE booking with members on Office365/Lark/CalDav, createAllCalendarEvents calls each member's credential but every credential writes to the first member's externalId (e.g. `/me/calendars/<first member's calendar>/events` with the second member's token), which fails auth/404 — so the PR's stated goal (collective multiple-host destination calendars) silently only works for google_calendar and non-Google members' events are lost.

[ADVISORY] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when destinationCalendar is null (the exact value this diff now assigns when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), so collected teamDestinationCalendars are discarded without any error or log. A COLLECTIVE booking where the event type and organizer have no destination calendar but members do drops all member calendars from evt, and event creation falls into the legacy create-all-credentials branch instead of honoring the members' selected destination calendars.

[BUG] Scope drift plus regression: the 'simplification' of the org-slug spread inverts the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition, so slug is now written when team billing is enabled instead of when it is disabled, in a file otherwise untouched by the destinationCalendar intent. Organizations created with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false (self-hosted/default) no longer get slug set on the organization record, breaking org routing/provisioning for every newly created organization; organizations created with billing enabled now get a slug they previously did not. Nothing in this PR's stated intent (collective multi-host destinationCalendar) requires touching organization creation at all.

[BUG] The array migration drops the optional chaining on the Meet fallback: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is evaluated without `?.` after `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`, so it crashes with TypeError exactly on the path the fallback exists for. A booking with location 'integrations:googlemeet' and no destinationCalendar (eventType and organizer have none — the exact scenario the 'Fallback to Cal Video' branch was written for) throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of degrading to Daily video, turning a bookable flow into a 500.

[BUG] updateEvent's calendar resolution is a tautology: in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined and always returns undefined, discarding the previous `destinationCalendar.externalId` fallback. Rescheduling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId now calls Google events.update with calendarId undefined (API error → update silently fails), whereas before this PR it updated the event on the destination calendar; the under-scoped migration replaced a working single-DC fallback with dead code.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same tautological find: when externalCalendarId is falsy the predicate `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` can never match, so calendarId resolves to undefined instead of the previous destinationCalendar.externalId fallback. Cancelling a legacy booking without a stored reference externalCalendarId no longer deletes the Google Calendar event (calendarId undefined → API error), leaving orphaned calendar events on every such cancellation.

[BUG] Under-scoped multi-host support: only GoogleCalendarService.createEvent was taught to select the destination calendar by credentialId; Office365, Lark, and BaseCalendarService still unconditionally use destinationCalendar[0] ('mainHostDestinationCalendar') even though EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now invokes createEvent once per host credential. For a collective booking with two Office365 (or Lark/Cal-DAV) hosts, EventManager loops over both hosts' destination calendars, but every createEvent call targets destinationCalendar[0] — the second host's token is used against the first host's calendar externalId, producing 404s or events created in the wrong host's calendar; the PR title's promise (collective multiple host) only holds for Google.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (set to null three lines above when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), so members' calendars are collected and then dropped. A COLLECTIVE event type where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do: teamDestinationCalendars is built, then discarded because push is skipped on null; the booking proceeds with no destination calendar array, so members' calendars never receive the event via the new per-destination loop.

[BUG] Scope drift: the loadUsers rewrite (a) silently removes `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user Prisma select and (b) wraps the whole loader in a catch that converts every non-HttpError failure into a 500 'Unable to load users' — neither is traceable to the destinationCalendar intent. Dynamic collective bookings lose user.organization on every loaded user, so any downstream consumer of user.organization.slug (org-branded handling on the booking path) now sees undefined; additionally, transient Prisma errors that previously surfaced with their real message now return a generic 500, changing API error behavior on an untouched requirement.

[BUG] The new COLLECTIVE feature reads `user.destinationCalendar` from users produced by loadUsers, whose select list (`userSelect.select` + credentials + metadata) is not shown to include destinationCalendar, so the feature's core input depends on an unverified select contract. If userSelect.select omits destinationCalendar, user.destinationCalendar is undefined for every host, teamDestinationCalendars stays empty, and the headline feature of this PR silently no-ops for all team-event bookings with no error — the author must confirm destinationCalendar is present in both the userSelect path and the eventType.users include path.

[BUG] In the created-results mapping, the non-calendar branch changed from `credentialId: result.credentialId` to `credentialId: undefined`, silently dropping the credential reference for non-calendar (video) results — a behavior change not traceable to the multi-host calendar intent. Video-app booking results (the branch handling meetingId/meetingUrl from createdEventObj) no longer carry the credential that created them; any consumer resolving a video booking's app credential by result.credentialId now gets undefined.

[ADVISORY] The credential-from-DB hydration block (prisma.credential.findUnique + manual Credential object construction) is copy-pasted into three places in this diff: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents, and handleCancelBooking — and the copies have already drifted (the handleCancelBooking copy omits the app-slug include the EventManager copies fetch). The next change to credential hydration (e.g., adding a field to the constructed Credential) must be made in three hand-maintained copies and the existing drift shows the copies are not kept in sync; a staff-level fix is one shared helper (e.g., getCredentialWithApp) making the extra branches unnecessary.

[ADVISORY] `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` is added to the CalendarEvent interface and set on evt in handleNewBooking, but no code in this diff ever reads evt.schedulingType — the COLLECTIVE decision is made inline from eventType.schedulingType before the event is built. An untraceable field expands the CalendarEvent surface that gets serialized into downstream payloads (emails, webhook bodies — note webhook.e2e.ts asserts exact payload shapes in this same PR) with no consumer, inviting drift between the payload and actual behavior; delete it or name its consumer.

[ADVISORY] Untraceable drive-by change: the hidden-notes string is edited from 'Notes have been hidden by the organiser' to '...organizer' inside the createEvent signature refactor, with no requirement in this PR covering user-facing copy. A user-visible string in calendar event notes changes silently in a bug-fix PR, which is review noise and untestable against any requirement; if the spelling fix is wanted it should be its own change with its own verification.

[BUG] The destructure `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` is followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining, so an empty or null destinationCalendar throws TypeError instead of reaching the Cal Video fallback. Any booking with location === MeetLocationType and no destination calendar (destinationCalendar null or []) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' — the old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` and safely fell back; now the whole booking flow throws.

[BUG] The spread condition was inverted: `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` became `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, flipping which billing mode sets slug and which sets metadata.requestedSlug. With team billing disabled (self-hosted default), organization creation no longer sets `slug` at all — organizations are created without a URL slug and existing flows that read org slug break; with billing enabled, slug is now written directly AND requestedSlug in metadata, contradicting the billing flow that previously only recorded requestedSlug pending payment.

[BUG] In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares cal.externalId against undefined and never matches, yielding selectedCalendar === undefined. Any updateEvent call without externalCalendarId (e.g. EventManager passing calenderExternalId=null for legacy references) now calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the event update fails against the wrong/undefined calendar, where the old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId; the dead find() was clearly meant to use mainHostDestinationCalendar.

[BUG] deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` is only evaluated when externalCalendarId is falsy, compares against undefined, and returns undefined so calendarId is undefined. Cancellation flows that delete a calendar event without an externalCalendarId now pass calendarId undefined to calendar.events.delete — the remote event is never deleted (or the call errors), leaving orphaned calendar events on every such cancellation.

[BUG] Office365CalendarService.createEvent (and LarkCalendarService.createEvent, and BaseCalendarService) were left on the old single-arg signature and read `event.destinationCalendar[0]` (the 'main host' entry) instead of the destination matching their own credentialId, which Google's new credentialId parameter now selects. For a COLLECTIVE booking with multiple Office365/Lark hosts, createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per destination, but every non-Google service creates every event in destinationCalendar[0] — host2's event is written to host1's calendar id using host2's credentials (wrong calendar or 404), so multi-host collective bookings only materialize in the first host's calendar.

[BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar both absent), even though teamDestinationCalendars was populated. For a collective event where the organizer has no default destination calendar but team members do, the members' collected destination calendars are computed and then silently discarded — no calendar events are created for any member, defeating the exact feature this PR adds, with no error surfaced.

[BUG] For destination-calendar entries without a credentialId (the legacy no-credentialId path in createAllCalendarEvents), `find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)` compares the entry's undefined credentialId against a real credential id, never matches, and selectedCalendar falls back to "primary". Bookings whose destinationCalendar row predates credentialId population (handled by the else-branch that iterates credentials by type) now create the Google event on the organizer's primary calendar instead of the user-selected destination calendar — a silent regression from the previous behavior that used destination.externalId directly.

[BUG] `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` now derives the booking reference's externalCalendarId from the createEvent return's `externalId` parameter, which is undefined for every createEvent call that doesn't pass a destination externalId (the no-credentialId destination branch and the fallback branch). BookingReference rows created for legacy destinations no longer carry externalCalendarId, so subsequent reschedule/cancel flows that look the event up by externalCalendarId cannot target the originally-selected calendar — the reference data required by the update/delete paths is silently lost at creation time.

[ADVISORY] A `prisma.credential.findUnique` query executes inside the `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop (and a second copy inside the per-reference loop in updateAllCalendarEvents), a query-in-loop pattern. One booking with N destinations issues N sequential credential queries instead of one `findMany({ where: { id: { in: ... } } })`; N is host-count-bounded today so it is latency, not a cliff, but the pattern is exactly the N+1 shape the codebase should not normalize.

[ADVISORY] The credential-from-DB fallback block is now hand-maintained in three places (createAllCalendarEvents, updateAllCalendarEvents, handleCancelBooking) with already-drifting shapes — handleCancelBooking's copy omits the app-slug include and the CredentialWithAppName field mapping the other two perform. The next change to credential hydration (e.g. adding a field getCalendar needs) must be replicated in three sites; a miss in one silently produces a malformed credential object on only one of the three code paths, and the drift is already visible in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The new per-reference loop wraps the pre-existing per-credential loop (and, in the recurring branch, a per-updatedBooking loop), producing a references × credentials × bookings fan-out of external deleteEvent API calls for one logical cancellation. A collective booking with several calendar references and several calendar credentials triggers N×M (recurring: N×M×K) external DELETE calls per cancellation, most of which target calendars the reference doesn't belong to and 404 — wasted external API quota and noisy failure logs that grow with host count.

[ADVISORY] The SchedulingType enum comparison was replaced with bare string literals — `["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)` and a separate `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` later in the same file — instead of the named enum (imported as a type in this very PR in Calendar.d.ts). A typo'd or renamed scheduling type string compiles cleanly and silently disables the collective destination-calendar push (the second literal feeds the exact branch this PR's feature depends on); the enum import exists precisely to make this compile-checked.

[BUG] The rewritten Google Meet fallback crashes with a TypeError when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, because mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and the code calls .integration on it without a guard. Any booking with location = Google Meet and no destination calendar (eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar both absent, or payment/confirm flows passing `destinationCalendar: []`) throws `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` instead of falling back to Cal Video — the exact scenario the original `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` check existed for, per its own comment 'Fallback to Cal Video if Google Meet is selected w/o a Google Cal'. The null-safe behavior was silently destroyed in this iteration.

[BUG] The spread condition for `slug` was silently inverted: previously `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` persisted the slug when team billing was DISABLED, now `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` persists it when billing is ENABLED. Organization creation behavior flips with the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED flag for an unrelated feature: with billing enabled, organizations now get both `slug` and `metadata.requestedSlug` set (previously only requestedSlug); with billing disabled, neither is set (previously slug was set). This is an unrelated objective change smuggled into a destinationCalendar fix, with no test covering organization creation in this diff.

[BUG] In updateEvent, the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find compares every cal.externalId against a falsy value and can never match, always returning undefined. Reschedules/updates of bookings whose stored reference has no externalCalendarId (exactly the legacy-reference case the old `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback served) now pass calendarId: undefined to calendar.events.update, so the update targets the wrong calendar or fails, instead of updating the event on the booking's destination calendar.

[BUG] In deleteEvent, the same broken pattern: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find can never match and calendarId is always undefined. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId no longer deletes the event from the booking's destination calendar (old code used destinationCalendar.externalId); the delete call gets calendarId undefined and the remote Google Calendar event is orphaned, leaving busy slots blocked on the attendee/organizer calendar.

[BUG] When neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists, evt.destinationCalendar is null and `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op, discarding the collected teamDestinationCalendars. For COLLECTIVE events where the organizer has no destination calendar but team members do, the members' calendars are collected in teamDestinationCalendars (lines ~990-996) and then silently dropped — no calendar events are created for any member, with no error or warning, contradicting the PR's stated intent of handling collective multiple-host destination calendars.

[ADVISORY] In createEvent, when no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed credentialId, the event silently falls back to calendarId "primary", whereas the old code used the stored destinationCalendar.externalId. Legacy destination rows without a credentialId (the case EventManager's else-branch still serves by calling createEvent(c, event) with no externalId) now create every Google event on the organizer's primary calendar instead of the user's selected destination calendar — bookings silently land in the wrong calendar with no error surfaced to the user.

[ADVISORY] In the no-credentialId destination branch, createEvent(c, event) is called without the externalId argument, so the returned EventResult has externalId undefined and the booking reference gets externalCalendarId: undefined. Bookings created through this branch lose their externalCalendarId reference entirely (previously populated from evt.destinationCalendar.externalId), which then feeds the broken undefined-externalId find() paths in Google updateEvent/deleteEvent and makes later reschedule/cancel unable to locate the created event.

[ADVISORY] The BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payload shape was silently changed from `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`, and the e2e test was edited in this PR to codify the new shape rather than flagging the contract change. Out-of-tree webhook consumers that branch on `payload.destinationCalendar === null` (or expect a single object) now receive an array for every booking without a destination calendar; the public webhook contract changed inside a bug-fix PR with no changelog, migration note, or versioning — external integrations break on deploy.

[ADVISORY] The loadUsers rewrite is unrelated scope creep for a destinationCalendar fix: it adds new throw paths (empty dynamicUserList, non-array hosts), a generic 500 catch, and silently drops `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` from the dynamic-user prisma select. Dynamic collective bookings where a downstream consumer reads user.organization?.slug now get undefined (data silently removed from the query in the same commit that claims to fix destination calendars); additionally the new 400/500 error paths for user loading were never part of the accepted objective and have no test coverage in this diff.

[ADVISORY] The 'fetch credential from DB and reshape into CredentialWithAppName' block is copy-pasted verbatim twice within this file (createAllCalendarEvents and updateAllCalendarEvents) and a third variant exists in handleCancelBooking.ts, instead of being extracted into one shared helper. The next change to credential fetching (e.g., adding a field to the reshaped object or handling credentials without an app row — where the code currently silently skips creating the calendar event because `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy) must be applied in three hand-maintained copies; the copies will drift exactly like the updateEvent/deleteEvent find() logic already did in this PR.

[BUG] The Google Meet fallback check dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without optional chaining, so it throws TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, whereas the old code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration and fell through to switching location to Cal Video. Any booking with location set to Google Meet and no destination calendar (the exact scenario this fallback exists for) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' and the booking fails with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

[BUG] evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is called when evt.destinationCalendar was just set to null three lines above (when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), so it calls push on null and throws. Every COLLECTIVE booking where the event type and organizer have no destination calendar fails with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading push)' — a 500 on the booking endpoint for a common configuration, not an edge case.

[BUG] updateEvent's fallback looks up event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) but this branch only runs when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it searches for an entry whose externalId equals undefined and always returns undefined. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, update previously targeted destinationCalendar.externalId; now selectedCalendar is undefined and calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined, so reschedule updates to the calendar event fail for legacy bookings.

[BUG] deleteEvent's calendarId fallback (event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId) is evaluated only when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it matches entries whose externalId === undefined and yields undefined instead of the old destinationCalendar?.externalId. Cancelling a booking whose reference lacks externalCalendarId calls calendar.events.delete with an undefined calendarId; the remote calendar event is never deleted and the orphaned Google Meet/event entry stays on the organizer's calendar.

[BUG] The new prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } }) lookup has no userId/teamId scope, whereas the previous code only used credentials from this.calendarCredentials (an ownership-scoped set), so any credential id referenced by a destinationCalendar record is loaded and its OAuth key used regardless of owner. The previous in-memory list acted as the ownership boundary; removing it means any code path that can influence destinationCalendar.credentialId (now including other members' calendars collected for COLLECTIVE events) causes event creation with an arbitrary user's stored credential key — a cross-tenant credential-use primitive if a destination calendar ever references a foreign credential id.

[BUG] The cancellation path now fetches the calendar credential via prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) with no userId scope, replacing the old lookup that was restricted to bookingToDelete.user.credentials. If a booking reference's credentialId ever points at another user's credential, the deleter uses that foreign credential (its OAuth token) to delete events on that user's calendar; the old code silently skipped such references, the new code actively uses them.

[BUG] For dynamic collective bookings (no eventTypeId), users are loaded from the request-supplied dynamicUserList and each listed user's destinationCalendar is pushed into teamDestinationCalendars, which then drives per-destination event creation using those users' credentials via the new unscoped DB credential fetch. A booker can compose a dynamic collective link naming arbitrary usernames and, by picking a slot where those users are free, cause calendar events (with the booker-controlled booking title) to be written into arbitrary users' personal calendars using their OAuth credentials — cross-user calendar writes driven by client-supplied input rather than by the event type owner.

[ADVISORY] The spread flip changes both flag states: slug is now written directly when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true (previously gated to requestedSlug-in-metadata until activation) and neither slug nor requestedSlug is written when it is false (previously slug was written). With billing enabled, organizations get an active public slug immediately at creation, bypassing the pending-slug/verification flow that metadata.requestedSlug exists for (slug squatting before payment/verification); with billing disabled (self-hosted), created organizations end up with no slug at all and the org URL flow breaks.

[ADVISORY] When no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined and the event silently falls back to calendarId 'primary' instead of the user-selected calendar. adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` changed the fallback from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The new prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } }) lookup has no userId/teamId scope, whereas the previous code only used credentials from this.calendarCredentials (an ownership-scoped set), so any credential id referenced by a destinationCalendar record is loaded and its OAuth key used regardless of owner. The previous in-memory list acted as the ownership boundary; removing it means any code path that can influence destinationCalendar.credentialId (now including other members' calendars collected for COLLECTIVE events) causes event creation with an arbitrary user's stored credential key — a cross-tenant credential-use primitive if a destination calendar ever references a foreign credential id.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds multiple unscoped credential fetches by raw id (e.g. `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`: `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: destination.credentialId } })`, and similarly in `updateCalendarEvent` and `handleCancelBooking`) and then uses the returned `key` to call calendar APIs. Previously, the code only used `this.calendarCredentials.find(...)`, which is an in-memory, pre-scoped set. In the new code, if an event’s `destinationCalendar[].credentialId` points to a credential not already in `this.calendarCredentials`, it will be loaded from the DB with no `userId`/`teamId` constraint and used. The diff also expands `destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE events, appends other users’ destination calendars (`handleNewBooking.ts`: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), increasing the surface where foreign `credentialId`s can be encountered. This creates a concrete cross-tenant credential-use risk if a `DestinationCalendar` record can reference an unintended credential id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The cancellation path now fetches the calendar credential via prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } }) with no userId scope, replacing the old lookup that was restricted to bookingToDelete.user.credentials. If a booking reference's credentialId ever points at another user's credential, the deleter uses that foreign credential (its OAuth token) to delete events on that user's calendar; the old code silently skipped such references, the new code actively uses them.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, the new logic handles `credentialId` references by first searching `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, but if not found it now falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then uses that credential to instantiate a calendar client and call `deleteEvent(...)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] For dynamic collective bookings (no eventTypeId), users are loaded from the request-supplied dynamicUserList and each listed user's destinationCalendar is pushed into teamDestinationCalendars, which then drives per-destination event creation using those users' credentials via the new unscoped DB credential fetch. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the new fallback for `selectedCalendar` in `updateEvent` is:

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] LarkCalendarService.createEvent uses `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) without matching on the credentialId passed under the new Calendar interface, unlike the Google implementation this diff adds. adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` and updates GoogleCalendarService to select the destination calendar by matching `credentialId` against `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar`. For Lark credentials, this means it will always use destinationCalendar[0] rather than the calendar matching the credential being processed, causing events to be created on the wrong calendar (or to throw `no calendar id` if the first destination is not a valid Lark calendar). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when evt.destinationCalendar is null (the value the ternary above assigns when neither eventType nor organizerUser has a destination calendar), discarding the teamDestinationCalendars just collected. adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`: null` in the ternary). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which becomes a silent no-op when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`. Since `teamDestinationCalendars` are collected from team members’ `user.destinationCalendar`, this path drops them entirely, and downstream `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` only iterates when `event.destinationCalendar && event.destinationCalendar.length > 0`, so those member calendars will be ignored.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The booking record connects only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` even when the diff's new collective flow populates several destination calendars and creates calendar events for all of them. For collective bookings, the persisted Booking.destinationCalendar relation under-represents the actual destinations (only the organizer/eventType's is linked); any consumer that reconstructs evt from booking.destinationCalendar — the pattern this diff itself repeats in bookingReminder, payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule handlers — sees only the first calendar, so future flows built on that relation will operate on one member's calendar while events exist on several.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a mismatch between the new multi-destination runtime model and what gets persisted on the Booking. In `handleNewBooking.ts`, collective/team logic can append multiple calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`), and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` to create events for each. The diff also continues to reconstruct `evt.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (wrapped into a single-element array) in multiple places (e.g., bookingReminder, payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/requestReschedule), which would only ever carry that single persisted destination. While the diff doesn’t conclusively prove an immediate broken flow (updates/deletes now primarily use calendar references), it is a concrete, diff-grounded inconsistency that can cause future/adjacent logic that relies on `booking.destinationCalendar` to under-operate (only the first calendar) despite events having been created on multiple calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` drops the optional chaining the old code had (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`), so a null/empty destinationCalendar crashes on `.integration` When Google Meet is selected without a Google calendar connected (destinationCalendar null — exactly the case the fallback comment describes, and the case handleNewBooking now produces by setting `destinationCalendar: ... : null`), booking creation throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the user gets a 500 instead of the intended Cal Video fallback

[];` and then unconditionally reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this throws `TypeError` on `.integration`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it searches for a calendar whose externalId equals undefined/null and always returns undefined For any booking reference without a stored externalCalendarId (legacy references, or references created by the new no-credentialId path), reschedule now calls `calendar.events.update` with `calendarId: undefined` where the old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`; the Google API call fails and the remote event keeps the old time while the booking reports success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, `selectedCalendar` is computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (null/undefined), the `.find(...)` compares each `cal.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` (i.e., null/undefined), so it will almost always return `undefined` rather than falling back to a real destination calendar externalId (the old behavior was `: event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This means `calendar.events.update` can be invoked with an undefined `calendarId` for references that don't have `externalCalendarId` stored (the call sites pass `calenderExternalId` which is set to `null` when missing in `EventManager.updateBooking`), leading to failed updates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In deleteEvent the same pattern `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it can never match and yields undefined Cancelling a booking whose calendar reference has no externalCalendarId now calls `calendar.events.delete` with `calendarId: undefined` (previously fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`); the delete fails and the orphaned event stays on the attendee's Google calendar while the cancellation flow completes

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` change the fallback calendar selection to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. Since that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is `undefined/null/""`, the `.find(...)` condition can never match a real destination calendar externalId, so the result is effectively always `undefined` (unless a calendar has an undefined externalId). This is a real logic defect introduced by the diff: it no longer reliably falls back to the event’s destination calendar when `externalCalendarId` is missing, which can cause deletes/updates to target the wrong calendar (or potentially an undefined calendarId depending on downstream usage).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Office365 createEvent was given a per-credential dispatch (CalendarManager now calls it once per destination with that credential) but still targets `event.destinationCalendar[0]` — the first/main-host calendar — instead of the calendar matching the credential being used For a COLLECTIVE booking with two Outlook members, the second member's credential is used to create/update the event in the first member's O365 calendar (duplicate on one calendar, none on the other's), or fails outright if the first destination is a non-O365 calendar whose externalId is invalid for the Graph API — while the booking reports success

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and changes `CalendarManager.createEvent` to call `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`, implying calendar services should select the destination calendar matching the credential being used. GoogleCalendarService was updated to `find` by `credentialId`, but Office365CalendarService was not: it still destructures the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];`) and uses that externalId for the Graph URL (`/me/calendars/${mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId}/events`). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, events are created per destination/credential, but the Office365 service will still target the first destination calendar regardless of which O365 credential is being used, causing wrong-calendar inserts or failures when the first destination isn’t the matching O365 calendar.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Lark createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent all use `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` — the first element — even though the manager now invokes them per-destination with a specific credential, so they never target the destination matching that credential In a collective booking mixing Lark with another calendar provider, the Lark credential writes into the main host's calendar id (or, if the first destination is non-Lark, `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` is a foreign id and createEvent throws 'no calendar id' logic on a mismatched externalId), leaving a member's Lark event missing or duplicated while the booking succeeds

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over each destination, selecting a specific credential per destination and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`. However, `CalendarManager.createEvent` does not pass `destination.externalId` into the calendar service; it only calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. GoogleCalendarService was updated to use `credentialId` to pick the matching destination (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but LarkCalendarService (and others) still do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and use that first element for create/update/delete. That means when multiple destination calendars are present (e.g., collective/team), the Lark credential may operate on the wrong destination (first element) rather than the one corresponding to that credential, causing missing/duplicated events or API errors. Additionally, LarkCalendarService's `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` signature no longer matches the updated `Calendar` interface requiring `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, which would fail type-checking/build.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the calendar list by `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (element [0]) instead of the destination matching the credential it is invoked with, ignoring the per-credential dispatch the PR introduces For a collective booking with multiple destinations handled by this service, every credential creates its event in the main host's calendar (or the filter matches nothing and events fan out to all calendars), so member calendars get duplicates/omissions while the booking API still reports success

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (BaseCalendarService), `createEvent` now derives `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then filters `calendars` by `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` (i.e., element `[0]`). But elsewhere in the diff (`packages/core/EventManager.ts`), collective/team flows build `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array (organizer first, then team members) and dispatch event creation per destination/credential. Using only the first destination’s `externalId` in BaseCalendarService will cause non-host credentials to either (a) create into the host’s calendar when the ID matches, or (b) filter out all calendars when it doesn’t (no event created), or (c) if no externalId, fan out to all calendars. This contradicts the per-credential/per-destination behavior introduced by the PR and can lead to duplicates/omissions while higher layers may still treat the attempt as successful.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` is a silent no-op when the preceding ternary set `destinationCalendar` to null (no eventType.destinationCalendar and no organizerUser.destinationCalendar), so the collected teamDestinationCalendars are discarded For a COLLECTIVE event where the organizer has no default calendar but team members do, the members' destination calendars are collected in teamDestinationCalendars and then silently dropped — no calendar event is created for anyone, with no error, no log, and no failed EventResult; the exact multi-host scenario this PR adds silently does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` is set via a ternary to either `[eventType.destinationCalendar]`, `[organizerUser.destinationCalendar]`, or `null` (when both are missing). Immediately after, for COLLECTIVE team events, the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The slug condition is inverted: the old `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` set the slug when billing was disabled, the new `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` sets it only when billing is enabled On every self-hosted/default deployment (IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false), organization creation succeeds but persists no slug, so the newly created org is unreachable at its /org/<slug> URL and any code reading organization.slug gets null — an operation that returns success while dropping required work

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the PR changes the organization `create` payload from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination's credentialId resolves to nothing (not in this.calendarCredentials, not found in DB, or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy) the destination is silently skipped — no log, no error, and no failed EventResult pushed to createdEvents The booking is created and reported successful while the calendar event for that destination is never created; for legacy credentials without an app relation the new DB-fetch fallback (added precisely to fix this) still drops the event invisibly, so users discover missing calendar entries only after the meeting is a no-show on that calendar

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the new loop over `event.destinationCalendar` only pushes a result when a `credential` is resolved and `createEvent(...)` runs. If `destination.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found in `this.calendarCredentials`, and the DB fallback (`prisma.credential.findUnique`) returns null or returns a row where `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is falsy, then `credential` remains undefined and the code falls through without logging and without pushing a failed `EventResult` (it simply skips that destination). This behavior is visible in the `if (credential) { ... createdEvents.push(...) }` block with no corresponding `else` handling for the unresolved-credential case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The updateAllCalendarEvents loop lacks the `if (credential)` guard that the parallel createAllCalendarEvents code has: after the in-memory filter and the new DB fetch fail, `credential` is undefined and is passed straight into `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` One unresolvable credential makes updateEvent throw; since the loop's promises are collected and awaited inside the surrounding try, the outer catch converts the failure into `appName: "none", success: false` results for every calendar reference — including ones whose updates actually succeeded — so the response misreports the whole reschedule as failed and hides which credential was broken

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents` (the reschedule/update path), inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop the code resolves `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials` and, if missing, attempts a DB fetch. But unlike `createAllCalendarEvents`, there is no `if (credential)` guard before calling `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))`. If both lookups fail, `credential` remains `undefined` and is passed into `updateEvent(...)`, which will likely throw/reject when it tries to use the credential. The surrounding `try/catch` then returns a failure result for every calendar reference (`calendarReference?.map(...)`), masking any successful updates and misreporting the overall outcome.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` (and the same at ~line 205) yields undefined for destinations without a credentialId, because that branch calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the externalId argument; the old code wrote `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` into the reference Bookings on legacy destinations without credentialId now get BookingReferences with a null/undefined externalCalendarId, which then flows into GoogleCalendarService update/delete where the falsy-id `find` fallback resolves undefined — the subsequent reschedule or cancel of those bookings targets calendarId undefined and fails (compounding the find-by-falsy-id regressions)

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows `CalendarManager.createEvent` now accepts `externalId?: string` and returns it as `externalId` in the `EventResult` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). `EventManager` now records booking references using `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` (packages/core/EventManager.ts ~lines 164 and ~203). However, in `createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch where a destination has **no `credentialId`** calls `createEvent(c, event)` without the `externalId` argument (packages/core/EventManager.ts in the `else` branch under `if (destination.credentialId)`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The loadUsers catch maps the thrown `new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` (a request-input problem) to `HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })` because only HttpError and PrismaClientKnownRequestError are re-thrown as 400 A booking request with an empty/invalid username list now receives a 500 'Unable to load users' where a 4xx with the real cause belongs, and the specific diagnostic message is discarded, misdirecting debugging toward server faults

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts`, `loadUsers` now wraps logic in a `try/catch`. When `!eventTypeId` and `dynamicUserList` is missing/empty, it explicitly throws `new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")`. The `catch` only converts `HttpError` or `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError` into a 400; any other `Error` is converted into `new HttpError({ statusCode: 500, message: "Unable to load users" })`, discarding the original message. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] After the new DB-fetch fallback for the calendar credential, if `prisma.credential.findUnique` still returns nothing the code falls through with `calendarCredential` undefined and the delete for that reference is silently skipped — no log, no entry in apiDeletes, no error in the response The cancellation API completes successfully while the remote calendar event for that reference is never deleted, leaving orphaned events on the organizer's calendar with zero server-side trace of why, making the reported 'delete failed silently' class of support tickets undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts`, inside the new loop over `bookingCalendarReference`, when `reference.credentialId` is set the code tries to find `calendarCredential` in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, then falls back to `prisma.credential.findUnique`. If that DB lookup also returns `null`, `calendarCredential` remains undefined and the code simply skips the deletion because it only proceeds under `if (calendarCredential) { ... apiDeletes.push(...) }` with no `else` logging or failure result.
